title: Replicating Safety Benchmark Results on Models Fine-Tuned with Different RLHF Variants
original_idea: Fine-tune a base model using DPO and ORPO on the same safety preference dataset. Evaluate both on HELM Safety and AILuminate. Identify whether RLHF algorithm choice meaningfully changes safety profiles.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Practical insight: if RLHF algorithm choice affects safety independently of training data, it should factor into safety-conscious training decisions. Directly actionable for practitioners.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model with two different RLHF algorithms (DPO, ORPO), understanding preference learning, and running evaluations. Significant ML engineering. Challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two separate fine-tuning runs plus evaluation on two benchmarks. Each fine-tuning run requires debugging and hyperparameter tuning. Too broad for 30 hours at beginner level.

novelty.reasoning: RLHF variant comparisons (PPO, DPO, ORPO) are well-studied for general performance. DPO exceeds PPO-based RLHF on sentiment control and matches or improves response quality (Rafailov et al., 2023). ORPO merges instruction-following and preference loss into one step. 'A Survey of Direct Preference Optimization' (arXiv:2503.11701, 2025) comprehensively reviews DPO variants. 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just A Few Tokens Deep' (OpenReview 2024) examines safety alignment depth. However, a controlled experiment training the same base model with DPO and ORPO on the same safety preference dataset and evaluating on HELM Safety and AILuminate to compare safety profiles has not been published. The specific safety-focused comparison is incrementally novel but the general comparison landscape is well-covered.

DPO.details: Confirmed: arXiv:2305.18290, NeurIPS 2023. Foundational method for preference optimization without reward modeling.

ORPO.details: Confirmed as a preference optimization method merging SFT and preference alignment. Referenced in multiple comparison studies.

HELM Safety.details: Confirmed at crfm.stanford.edu/helm/safety. Stanford CRFM safety evaluation benchmark.
